questions.q: What share of diagnosed work-related heat claims reach benefit payment?
questions.have: JKK benefits exist; heat-specific acceptance and delay were not verified. [I5, I6]
questions.could: Prospective multi-site claims pathway study, publishing aggregate submitted, accepted and paid counts and time intervals.
questions.scale: Illustrative: several provinces over two hot seasons; sample based on case volume.

questions.q: Does contribution support keep informal workers insured through the hot season?
questions.have: A registration experiment and a new contribution-saving route exist. [I16, I9]
questions.could: Cluster randomisation of assisted contribution-saving access, measuring active coverage, care costs and retention in aggregate.
questions.scale: Illustrative: 40-60 clusters; final size from power calculations.

questions.q: Does a pre-heat top-up reduce income loss, debt and delayed care?
questions.have: PKH delivery and general economic evaluations exist, without a verified heat effect. [I4, I17]
questions.could: Pre-specified phased top-up trial using forecasts, with household outcomes reported only in aggregate.
questions.scale: Illustrative: two hot seasons across 40-60 clusters.

questions.q: Which heat-related crop losses meet AUTP damage rules and receive timely support?
questions.have: Drought insurance terms and extension routes are published. [I11]
questions.could: Crop-season panel combining weather, field loss assessment and anonymised aggregate claim outcomes, without publishing farm locations.
questions.scale: Illustrative: 1,000-1,500 insured and comparable uninsured farm households.

questions.q: Do cash transfers reach families before or after the hottest weeks, and is the amount enough to cover lost work?
questions.have: Government reports count the families paid each quarter, without payment dates set against heat or amounts set against losses.
questions.could: Link payment dates with heat records and a short household survey on lost work and spending.
questions.scale: Illustrative: about 500 families in two provinces over one year

questions.q: Where do informal workers stop between hearing of worker insurance and applying for it?
questions.have: An evaluation in Bandung and Medan measured enrolment: registration help raised it by 3.5 percentage points and full subsidy by 18.6, while information alone had no measured effect. Awareness, documents and applications were not measured as separate steps.
questions.could: Follow the same workers through awareness, documents and application, with and without help to register.
questions.scale: Illustrative: about 1,000 workers in two cities
